analysis.title: Market Intelligence: US Morning Update (2 November 2026)
key_insights: Asia was mixed Monday after Friday's sharp US loss. Weak October PMIs in China (official manufacturing and non-manufacturing fell, unofficial manufacturing edged down) and India (manufacturing declined modestly but stayed in expansion), yet China, India and Korea stocks traded notably higher.
GS economists' 2026Q4 China investor survey suggests growth stays largely stable over the next six months, with risks skewed toward deceleration rather than acceleration.
South Korea's October exports showed a smaller than expected pullback on further chip export gains, which GS cites as the AI trade still being evident.
European equities are little changed while oil pulls back about 5% and rates markets are benign.

Daan Struyven raised GS oil forecasts: Brent $105 in December and an average of $88 for 2027. The base case now assumes 1 mbpd of consistently disrupted oil activity through 2027 even though Middle East flows have improved. Upside risk is $140/bbl Brent if Gulf supply stays constrained, downside into the $60s if output recovers faster.

Midterm election preview (Alec Phillips): prediction markets imply Democrats win the House with a wider margin, Senate control is uncertain. Fiscal deadlines (spending authority extension, debt limit increase) would be the main focus for legislation and could force compromise. Likely Democratic agenda items: the war in Iran, tariff rollback, reversal of spending cuts, expansion of health benefits.

GS adds Amphenol (APH) to the US Conviction List. Data center product mix is growing strongly while the company keeps a presence in Industrial and Military markets. The debate is whether APH stays relevant as the market shifts from copper to fiber optic connectors. GS expects IT Datacom to grow over 60% again in 2027, and sees the January CommScope acquisition plus durable copper uses sustaining APH's position. No stocks were removed from the US list.

European Conviction List adds Deutsche Bank and Carlsberg and removes HSBC, Haleon and CTP. APAC list adds Elite Material, Yokohama Rubber and JSW Steel and removes NYPCB, Shengyi Tech and Hong Kong Exchanges.

Snider's midseason earnings update: with 60% of the S&P 500 reported, 3Q26 EPS growth is on track for 33% y/y, matching 2Q. GS expects growth to slow to 18% in 2027. Earnings growth is strong but no longer accelerating. Key item to watch is continued acceleration in hyperscaler cloud revenues.

Chevron (CVX, Buy): 3Q beat on Friday driven by US production above 2 MBOE/d, record refinery throughput of 1.09 mbd, and Bakken midstream costs set to halve. GS expects 10%+ annual FCF/EPS growth through 2030 at $70/b Brent plus $2.5-3bn in buybacks and dividend growth. 12m price target raised to $256 from $241.

Oil E&Ps (Mehta): GS anchors coverage to a $73/bbl mid-cycle WTI price and sees a 12% average 2027/28 FCF yield. Best positioned are Buy-rated OXY (on the Conviction List), PR and DVN. Note says E&Ps are well positioned even at long-term $70-$75/bbl WTI.
ExxonMobil (XOM, Neutral): first take notes an EPS beat driven by refining, with focus on capital allocation priorities and LNG projects.

LPL Financial (LPLA, Buy): GS says buy the dip after 3Q results (reported Oct-27). Net new asset growth is below steady-state, with a credible path back to 5%-6% growth in 2027-2028 as recruiting normalizes, pipelines convert and Commonwealth re-enters the market. 12m price target $400.

Rating changes: Floor & Decor (FND) downgraded to Sell from Neutral on moderating 2027 unit growth and lowered FY26 guidance amid macro pressures. British American Tobacco upgraded to Buy from Neutral (Imperial remains Buy). Kia cut to Neutral from Buy and Skshu Paint to Sell from Buy.
Key data this week is Friday's employment report. Today: October ISM Manufacturing and S&P Global's October US manufacturing PMI, plus Chicago Fed President Goolsbee speaking at 11:15 AM.
Earnings before the open today: EL, MAR, CHH, L, FOX, CHKP, PEG, ETR, KOS, KRYS, IDXX. After the close: AAPL, ON, PLTR, SBAC, O, UDR, WMB, FANG, CLX, VRTX and others.

Other notes listed: G10 inflation monitor says core inflation accelerates outside Canada while trimmed measures look more benign; Global Data Center Capacity update raises capacity estimates; AI Adoption Tracker shows adoption at 24.6% in October 2026; Howmet (HWM, Buy) cites strength in operating performance and end markets; memory pricing tracker raises 4Q26 DRAM ASP forecast for PC, server/mobile in line, NAND lower than GS estimates.
